Volumetric illustration differs from surface-based NPR in several important ways [S2, S4, unofficial].

In surface NPR, surfaces (features) are well-defined, whereas with volumes, feature areas within the volume must be determined through analysis of local volumetric properties because volumetric features vary continuously throughout three-dimensional space [S2, S4, unofficial].
Stylization in volume rendering emerged from the need to convey complex internal structures that are often obscured in traditional volume rendering.
Early work focused on adapting surface-based NPR techniques, such as hatching and stippling, to volumetric data.
Stipple Volume Rendering was introduced to address the specific challenges of volumetric feature detection, such as the lack of well-defined surfaces [S2].
These methods are primarily used in scientific visualization and medical imaging to highlight specific anatomical or physical features through artistic abstraction [S2, unofficial].
